## Proof

We work in the posets $(\mathcal{P}(B), \subseteq)$ and $(\mathcal{P}(A), \subseteq)$. Recall that for $V \subseteq B$ the inverse image is
$$f^{-1}(V) = \{a \in A \mid f(a) \in V\},$$
and we write $f^{-1}(b)$ as shorthand for the fiber $f^{-1}(\{b\}) = \{a \in A \mid f(a) = b\}$.

To show that $f_{*}: \mathcal{P}(A) \to \mathcal{P}(B)$, defined by
$$f_{*}(U) = \{b \in B \mid f^{-1}(b) \subseteq U\},$$
is the **right adjoint** of $f^{-1}: \mathcal{P}(B) \to \mathcal{P}(A)$, we must establish the adjunction
$$f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U \iff V \subseteq f_{*}(U)$$
for all $V \in \mathcal{P}(B)$ and $U \in \mathcal{P}(A)$.

---

### $(\Rightarrow)$: $f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U \implies V \subseteq f_{*}(U)$

Assume $f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U$. Let $b \in V$. Since $\{b\} \subseteq V$, monotonicity of $f^{-1}$ gives
$$f^{-1}(b) = f^{-1}(\{b\}) \subseteq f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U.$$
Hence $f^{-1}(b) \subseteq U$, which is precisely the defining condition for $b \in f_{*}(U)$. Since $b \in V$ was arbitrary, $V \subseteq f_{*}(U)$.

### $(\Leftarrow)$: $V \subseteq f_{*}(U) \implies f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U$

Assume $V \subseteq f_{*}(U)$. Let $a \in f^{-1}(V)$, so that $f(a) \in V$. By the assumption, $f(a) \in f_{*}(U)$, which by definition means
$$f^{-1}(\{f(a)\}) \subseteq U.$$
Since $a \in f^{-1}(\{f(a)\})$ (because $f(a) = f(a)$), we obtain $a \in U$. As $a \in f^{-1}(V)$ was arbitrary, $f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U$.

---

### Conclusion

Both implications hold, so for all $V \subseteq B$ and $U \subseteq A$,
$$f^{-1}(V) \subseteq U \iff V \subseteq f_{*}(U).$$
This is exactly the statement that $f^{-1} \dashv f_{*}$, i.e. $f_{*}$ is the right adjoint of the inverse image operation $f^{-1}$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
